Commentary.Commentary: We are moments away from the run chase! Bismah Maroof is seen motivating her team in a huddle. The umpires are followed by the Pakistan players to the middle. Out come the dynamic-duo of Alyssa Healy and Rachael Haynes as they are set to open the innings. Diana Baig is set to start proceedings with the new ball. Let's play...

Craig McMillan is out there with an update on the Pitch. The heavy roller has been used during the break, he informs. He shows that there are no footmarks on the surface and the spin that Australia got was from the main body of the pitch. He is very interested to see how the Aussies will bat against the Pakistan spinners and so are we!
... The Run Chase ...

Right then! Pakistan Women have just 190 runs to defend but they have quality spinners in the side that can trouble the best of batters and on a pitch that is fairly slow, they might just have a chance. Australia Women though will be looking to just get out and play their strokes and chase down the target as soon as possible. Do join us in a short while for the chase.

Aliya Riaz comes up for a quick chat. Says that she is very happy with her performance and tells that she works on her basics and has executed them well in the match. Shares that the plan was to stay in the middle and build a partnership. Feels that there is help for the spinners and hopes for the best in the second innings.

Pakistan Women were reeling at 44/4 but the skipper stood up when it mattered the most and Bismah Maroof guided her side to a below-par but defendable total. Sidra Ameen and her new opening partner Nahida Khan had fallen in quick succession early on. Omaima Sohail gave good support to the skipper but couldn't hang on for long. Nida Dar soon followed Sohail but then came Aliya Riaz. Since the start of 2020, no one has scored more runs than her, batting at number 6 or 7. Slowly but surely, Maroof and Riaz created inroads and put on a 99-run stand as both the batters crossed the individual fifty-run mark. Riaz fell but Maroof stayed until the end and ended up with 78 runs.

On a slow track, Megan Schutt and Ellyse Perry made a good start with the new ball. Schutt in particular was impressive and the pair picked up a wicket each to put the opposition on the back foot. The two leggies then came on after the Powerplay and Alana King as well as Amanda-Jade Wellington too picked up a wicket each very early on in their spell. After that though, the spinners were only able to stem the flow of runs and for almost 30 odd overs, Australia failed to pick up a wicket. The wicket did come and it was Carey who got the breakthrough but she was quite expensive at the death. King came back in late to pick up her second wicket but Schutt couldn't quite close out the innings as well as she would have wanted to.

It has been a tremendous fightback from Pakistan Women and they have somehow managed to get to 190 runs. This is by no means a par total but it is the effort that will give them a lot of hope when they come out to bowl. Australia Women though will feel fairly comfortable chasing it down even though they failed to pick up wickets in the middle overs.

FOUR! Great shot to end the innings! Megan Schutt lands it on a fuller length, around middle, Bismah Maroof steps back to make room and smashes it through the gap between mid off and extra cover. 12 from the over, Pakistan Women end on 190/6!
Very full and around off, Diana squeezes it out through mid off for a single.
FOUR! Clean hitting! Fuller in length, around off, Diana Baig goes full monty, swings her bat at it and powers it over square leg for a boundary.
A full ball on middle, Maroof swings it to deep mid-wicket for just a single.
Full and on middle, Maroof tries to whip it on the leg side but misses. It hits her on the pads and rolls beside the pitch. The non-striker wants a run but is sent back.
Wide! Megan tries to follow the batter down the leg side but ends up slipping it way too wide.
Around off, on a length, it's dragged over to deep mid-wicket for one.
Megan Schutt (9-1-31-1) will bowl the final over of the innings.
A yorker outside off, dug out to point.
Tucks it to square leg for a single.
Diana Baig is in at number 8.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! A floated leg spinner, landing around leg and turning away sharply, Fatima Sana goes down one knee to sweep but fails to middle her shot properly. There is a faint tickle and Alyssa Healy shows good reflexes to catch it. She initially looks to take the bails off but then stops and appeals. The finger goes up!
Commentary.Howout: c Alyssa Healy b Alana King

Commentary.Commentary: Short and around off, Sana walks forward and then goes back to cut but misses. The bails are taken off but Fatima is safely in.
Fullish and on middle, Maroof skips down the track and pushes it to covers for a brisk run.
Flatter and fuller on middle, knocked down to long on for a run.
Interesting choice. Alana King (8-0-21-1) to bowl the penultimate over of the innings.

NOT OUT! Full and flighted, around leg, Fatima clips it to short fine leg and goes for a run. She is a bit casual in planting her bat inside the line and Nicola Carey has come up with a direct hit at the bowler's end. They appeal, it's referred upstairs but the replay finds Fatima Sana just safe.

Is that run out? Nicola Carey scores a direct hit at the bowler's end and it looks really close. The third umpire is called into action. The replays roll in and we can see that Fatima Sana just about made it home in time. NOT OUT!
Full and around leg, Bismah Maroof goes down and sweeps it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Loopy and full, around off, Sana walks forward a bit and eases it to extra cover for a run.
Full and flat, on the pads, swept to fine leg for one.
Tossed up around off, swept through square leg for a single.
Walks forward and chips it over mid on for a single.
Jess Jonassen (9-0-27-0) comes back in to finish her spell.
In the region around off, lofted down to long on for a couple.
Sliding down the leg side, Maroof nudges it to fine leg for a run.
Angling in around middle, it's knocked down to long on for a single.
FOUR! Too full in length and outside off, Fatima Sana throws her bat at it and slices it over point for a boundary.
Short and wide outside off, cut to point for a single.

NOT OUT! A yorker-length ball wide outside off, Maroof squeezes it out from the bottom part of her bat and it lobs behind to the keeper. Bismah leaves her crease and then tries to drag her foot back in. It though gets stuck before the crease and then she tries to land her back foot over the line. Alyssa Healy though fumbles while collecting the ball but it eventually falls on the stumps to dislodge the bails. The appeal for a run out is made. The third umpire has a few replays to watch and she gives the benefit of the doubt to the batter.

Is that out? The only thing that can warrant a wicket on a Free Hit is a run-out and that might have just happened here. Alyssa Healy doesn't collect it cleanly behind the stumps and after a couple of juggles, the ball pops out of her gloves and dislodges the bails. This seems to be really close as the foot seems to be up in the air when the bails come off. Hard to tell though, the third umpire is having a good hard look at it. The decision is made and it is NOT OUT!

FOUR! It's another beamer from Nicola Carey. A high full toss outside off, Bismah Maroof does well to get on top of the bounce as she glides it down to third man for a boundary. Called a no ball and Free Hit will follow.
Too full and on middle, it's eased to mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Gorgeous! Full and around off, angling away, Maroof leans forward and lofts it over extra cover for a boundary. 150 up!
Fuller and on off, pushed to mid off.
Uses the angle of the bowler and works it to mid-wicket.

Stumping chance, missed! Angling down the leg side, Fatima Sana tries to flick but misses and in the process leaves the crease. Alyssa Healy though has failed to collect the ball. It hit the outside of her gloves and slipped out.

Fatima Sana has reviewed the LBW decision in an instant! The third umpire deems it close to the bat and on checking with UltraEdge, there is a huge spike as the ball goes past the bat. The ball seemed to be sliding down leg but the deflection made it straighten. Good review from Sana and she survives.

NOT OUT! There is a spike on the UltraEdge. It's on a length, around off and angling in, Sana tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The appeal is made and the finger has gone up. It's reviewed instantly and the UltraEdge detects some wood.
Slower one, sliding onto the pads. Maroof gets an inside edge as she looks to flick.
Full and on off, pushed towards mid off for a quick single.
Length this time, angling into middle. Bismah Maroof heaves it towards deep mid-wicket for one. The Free Hit doesn't prove costly for Australia.

NO BALL! Oh, dear! What in the world was that? Carey looks for another change-up delivery but gets it horribly wrong and ends up serving it down the leg side and around head height. The ball eludes the keeper and the batters scamper through for a couple of byes as well. Free Hit to follow.
A full toss on middle, Fatima tucks it to mid-wicket for a single.
Fatima Sana is the new batter at number 7.

OUT! LBW! The partnership has finally been broken and that too on 99! This is bowled on a length, around middle and it might have been a knuckleball from Nicola Carey. The ball pitches, nips in a bit and finds a way through. Aliya Riaz looks to defend it with a straight bat but the ball goes through the gap between bat and pad to hit the back leg. Huge shout from the Aussies and the finger is raised up in an instant. Riaz does review it and the UltraEdge confirms there's no bat on it. Ball Tracking shows up three reds and Aliya Riaz has to depart after a gritty fifty.

DRS time! Aliya Riaz has been adjudged lbw. She looks at her skipper and then takes the referral. Doesn't appear there is any bat, the UltraEdge confirms the same. Ball Tracking shows that it's hitting the leg stump. It's all over for Aliya.
Drifted onto the pads, worked through square leg for a run.
This is pushed wider, Riaz looks to go over covers but mistimes it.

FOUR! Nicely played and fifty comes up for Aliya Riaz - her 5th in ODIs and first in the 50-over World Cup. This is a length ball, sliding down the leg side, Riaz just gets inside the line of the ball and eases it down to the fine leg fence.
Full, around middle and leg, pushed towards mid on.
Fuller in length, on middle and leg. This is driven through mid-wicket for another single.
Schutt comes from 'round the wicket and angles it across the off stump. Riaz nudges it towards backward point for a single.
A leg cutter, this is pushed well wide of the off stump line. Riaz tries to slash at it but cannot reach it. Good take from Alyssa Healy though.
Bowling change. Megan Schutt (7-1-19-1) returns for her third spell.
Pitched up, on middle, Bismah Maroof drives it firmly back towards the bowler who does well to get down low and make a partial stop.
Full and wide, edged down to backward point.
Full and slanting into leg stump. Riaz makes a bit of room and heaves it towards deep mid-wicket for one more.
Slower delivery, sliding onto the pads. Maroof with a tuck 'round the corner for a single.
A length ball, on off. Maroof hangs back and strokes it towards point.
WIDE! This is spilled down the leg side. Wide signalled.
This is angled into the pads. Maroof uses her feet to work it towards deep mid-wicket. The batters push hard for two and Maroof returns on strike. It's important for her to target the boundaries now.
Change in bowling. Nicola Carey is brought back into the attack. Just 12 runs from her 5 overs so far. Very economical.
This is floated up, full and down the leg side. Riaz looks to sweep it fine but the ball comes off the gloves and luckily for Riaz, it doesn't go on to hit the leg stump.
A stifled appeal for lbw from the bowler and nothing more. Around leg and sliding across. Riaz puts out a big stride forward as she looks to sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Quicker delivery, around off. Aliya Riaz rocks back and cuts it straight to the fielder at point.
Around leg stump, Maroof uses her feet and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter, around middle. This is worked through square leg for a single. This is now the highest partnership for any wicket for Pakistan Women in a 50-over World Cup match.
Around off, played towards cover.
Edged but just short! This is short and wide, turning away. Aliya Riaz looks to cut hard but gets a top edge which lands in front of a diving Rachael Haynes at short third man. Single taken.
On middle, pushed through mid on for one.

FOUR! Fifty up for the Pakistan skipper - her first after the maternity break, informs the on-air commentator. What a captain's innings this has been so far! Quicker, sliding across off. Bismah Maroof hangs back and cuts it really late to get it past short third man and picks up a boundary. She would be aiming to finish strongly here.
Maroof steps down the track again and Wellington just slows it up. Maroof plays it towards mid-wicket. Three dots in a row now.
On middle, Maroof nudges it towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up, around off. Maroof skips down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
The umpire signals the start of Powerplay 3 which will last from overs 41-50. As many as 5 fielders can be kept outside the inner ring.
And again. Short and around off, Aliya gets back to cut. It takes the outer half and goes straight to short third man. Just 1 from the over.
Short and on off, turning away, Aliya cuts but finds the point fielder.
Tossed up, on middle, helped to mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, swept to fine leg for one.
Flatter and around off, defended back to the bowler from the crease.
Quicker and around off, turned on the leg side, straight to square leg.
Swing and a miss! Loopy and around off, spinning away, Aliya Riaz goes down to slog sweep but misses.
Fuller and on middle, knocked down to long on for a run.

SAFE! Full and around off, Maroof reverse-sweeps it to short third man and looks for a run. Again Riaz sends her back and she returns. The throw comes to the keeper who jumps to collect the ball and breaks the stumps. The appeal is made, it's referred upstairs but Bismah Maroof is found to be safe in the replays.

Is that a run-out? Alyssa Healy doesn't seem interested but the appeal is made and the umpire has gone upstairs. The replays show that the throw was a bit too high and Healy had to reach for it. This allowed Bismah Maroof the time to get back into the crease before the bails were whipped off. NOT OUT!
Lunges to a full ball and pushes it to cover-point. Maroof wants a run but her partner is not ready.
Shortish and on off, cut through cover-point for a run.
Flighted and full on middle, Riaz walks forward and pushes it to mid on.
Tossed up, on middle, Aliya Riaz bends one knee and sweeps it to fine leg for a single.
Beaten! Full and flighted, around off, Aliya Riaz again tries to defend but this one lands and straightens to beat the outside edge.
Loopy and landing full around off, Aliya Riaz presses forward in defense.
Quicker and flatter outside off, Riaz mistimes her drive to point.
Full and served down the leg side, swept to fine leg for a single.
Too full and around middle, Bismah Maroof forces it down towards mid on where Rachael Haynes makes a good partial stop.
Aerial but safe! Floated and full, landing around off, Aliya Riaz drives it a bit uppishly but wide of the short cover fielder.
Tossed up, full and around off, pushed with the spin to short cover.
Flighted and full around off, Bismah Maroof flicks past the diving mid-wicket fielder for a single.
A dipping low full toss on middle, it's eased down to fine leg for a single.
Loopy around off, another full toss, this time Maroof works it wide of short mid-wicket and collects a single.
A low full toss around off, dipping in, Maroof walks forward and flicks it to short mid-wicket.
Uses her feet to take it on the full and knocks it down to mid on for a single.
Loopy and full, around off from 'round the wicket, Bismah Maroof defends it back off the front foot.
Quicker and on off, punched back to the bowler.
Flatter this time, short and wide, Maroof plays it down to point. Looks for a run but it's not on.
Turning away from the batter, on the shorter side, Aliya cuts to deep cover-point for one.
Flighted one, a touch short and on off, Riaz cuts but finds point.

Drinks break! Steady going for Pakistan Women after losing four wickets in a hurry. Bismah Maroof and Aliya Riaz have formed a strong alliance and their stand has helped Pakistan Women to recover from a precarious situation. They can't relax now as this is the last recognized pair and playing out the entire 50 overs should be on their agenda. Australia Women have maintained a firm hand on the game, keeping the scoring rate under check but would love to break this partnership and get into the vulnerable lower order of Pakistan.
Shorter in length and there's width on offer again. Riaz cuts it hard to deep cover for just a single.
Tossed up, around middle. Bismah Maroof dances down the track and drills it towards long on to pick up a single.
Flatter this time and sliding down the leg side. Aliya Riaz looks to pull it behind but edges it down to fine leg for another single.
Around off, pushed towards cover.
Fuller this time, outside off and this is cut away towards backward point.
Outside off and spinning away from the right-hander. Riaz plays it towards point.
Another bowling change. Jess Jonassen makes way for Amanda-Jade Wellington (4-1-11-1).
Short, well outside off and turning away. Riaz reaches out and slaps it to deep point for a run. 8 from the over, the most Pakistan Women have earned from an over in this match thus far.
FOUR! Aliya Riaz looking to up the ante now! This is on middle, Riaz steps out and heaves it aerially towards the wide long on fence for a boundary.
Shorter in length, outside off and turning away. Riaz taps it towards backward point.
Flighted this time, around middle and leg. Bismah Maroof uses her feet to get to the pitch of the ball and eases it down to long on for one.
Tossed up, on middle, Maroof pushes it towards mid off.
King starts off her spell with a loosener down the leg side. Maroof paddles it fine, past short fine leg and picks up a couple of runs.
Change in bowling. Alana King returns to bowl. 1 for 13 in her 7 overs so far.
Flatter this time, on off. Riaz goes on the back foot and dabs it down towards backward point.
A touch shorter this time and once again Riaz cuts it straight to the fielder at point.
Flatter delivery, angled in from well outside off. Riaz rocks back and cuts it straight to backward point.
Bismah Maroof getting funky now. On a length, around off. Maroof looks to reverse sweep but doesn't quite get the connection. She still picks up a single towards the point region.
Tossed up, on middle, Maroof nudges it on the leg side.
Quicker delivery, on off. Bismah Maroof gets right behind the line of the ball to block it.
Jess Jonassen to continue...
Slower delivery, on a length and sliding into middle and leg. Riaz looks to press forward and drive through mid on but mistimes it to the right of the bowler.
On middle this time, Riaz pushes it gently towards mid on.
Maroof once again backs away a bit. Schutt angles it around leg and this is worked through mid-wicket for one more.
A length ball, around off. Riaz taps it towards point for a quick run. The 100 is up!
Maroof makes a bit of room and Schutt tries to follow her. Maroof is able to flick it towards fine leg for a single.
On off, nudged towards cover-point.
Uses her feet and knocks a full ball down to long on for a single.
Quicker and flatter, around off. Maroof looks to drop and run but the fielder at point is quick to react.

FOUR! The first sign of aggression from Bismah Maroof and she picks up a boundary as well. Tossed up, on middle, Maroof slogs it uppishly through the gap between mid on and mid-wicket for a boundary. The 50 partnership also comes up between these two.
On middle, worked towards mid-wicket.
Here comes the arm ball. On off and angling in sharply. Riaz hops back and tucks it 'round the corner for a single.
Aliya Riaz steps out looking to be aggressive but Jess Jonassen cleverly pushes it wider. Riaz checks her shot and defends it out.
Fuller again, outside off, Maroof pushes it without much timing to the cover fielder.
Fuller and on off, defended watchfully by the Pakistan skipper.

EDGY FOUR! Megan Schutt lands it on a length around off and gets it to nip back in with some extra bounce. Bismah Maroof tries to defend but it takes the inside edge, beats the stumps and races behind for a boundary at fine leg.
Full and on off, angling in, Bismah Maroof presents a straight bat in defense.
Short in length, wide outside off, Aliya cuts it past the diving fielder at backward point for a single.
Begins her new spell from 'round the wicket for the left-hander, it's on a length around off, Maroof turns it towards square leg for a run.
Megan Schutt (5-1-10-1) is brought back into the attack.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Aliya Riaz is forward in defense.
Strides forward to a full ball and pushes it softly to covers.
Full and on middle, defended back.
Flatter and around off, defended on the off side.
Full and flighted on middle, it's sweep to deep square leg for a run.
Flighted and full on middle, flicked to mid-wicket.
Around middle, on a length, defended back.
Fuller and on off, pushed to covers.
Short and outside off, Aliya Riaz tries to cut but misses.

Shout for an lbw, the umpire remains unmoved! Perhaps going down the leg side. Alyssa Healy is heard saying - Umpire's call. Fuller in length, around middle and leg, it beats the straight defensive bat of Aliya Riaz and pings her on the front pad. The appeal is not entertained, Meg Lanning doesn't take the DRS and the Ball Tracking later shows that it's missing the leg stump by a long way.
Short and wide outside off, cut straight to the point fielder.
Fuller and on off, it's flicked in front of square leg for a single.

Bismah Maroof seems to be getting some pain relief spray on her right hand. Alyssa Healy too seems to have hurt her fingers and the physio is out to have a look. Everything seems fine and we are good to continue.

Flighted and around off, Maroof helps it around the corner and takes a single as the ball rolls towards square leg. The stand is worth 40 runs now, quite slow but that's the need of the hour for Pakistan Women as this is the last recognized batting pair.
Fullish and around off, Maroof tries to sweep but fails to middle her shot properly. It rolls beside the pitch.
Short and on off, punched off the back foot to sweeper cover for a single.
Flatter and shorter on off, Riaz taps it down to backward point and looks for a run. Sent back.
Loopy and full, around off, it's defended back off the inner half of the bat.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Jonassen starts with a delivery on the shorter side outside off, Aliya rocks back and whacks it through backward point for a boundary.
Jess Jonassen (1-0-6-0) is back on.
Fullish and outside off, pushed to covers to end the over.
Drags the length short, outside off, it's cut to the left of backward point for a quick run.
Uppish but safe! Full and on middle, Aliya Riaz is early into her defense and pushes it back uppishly. It doesn't carry back to the bowler.
Slower one, on a length around off, Maroof plays late and works it to square leg for a single.
Fuller in length, around middle and angling in from 'round the wicket, Maroof pushes it down to mid on.
Short and wide outside off, Aliya cuts it past the diving backward point fielder for a single.

Floated but down the leg side. Riaz gets inside the line of the ball and paddles it to fine leg for a single. Another tidy over from Alana King and Pakistan Women just looking to preserve wickets at the moment.
Very full, on off. Riaz jams it out towards cover.
On a length, around off. Riaz goes on the back foot and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Tossed up, on off. Pushed towards covers.
This is just a bit short and around off. Aliya Riaz hops back and cuts it late but can't get it past backward point.
Full and on off. This is pushed back towards the bowler.
A touch fuller, sliding in from around off. Maroof strokes it back towards the bowler.
Length this time, on off. This is driven but straight towards mid off.
Carey comes 'round the wicket and angles it in from around off. Bismah Maroof presents a dead bat to defend it out.
Good running! This is angled into middle, Riaz makes a bit of room and taps it towards the cover region for a quick single.
Around the top of off. This is worked towards cover-point.
On a driving length, outside off. Riaz looks to cover drive but the ball skids through and beats the outside edge of her blade.
Loopy delivery, on middle and off, possibly the wrong 'un. Aliya Riaz tries to defend off the front foot but it goes off the inner half of the bat behind square on the leg side, for a run.
There's a bit of width on offer this time and Aliya Riaz rocks back to cut. She can't beat the fielder at point though.
Tossed up, on off and played with the spin towards cover.
On a length, around off and turning away. Riaz hangs back and nudges it towards point.
A bit flighted this time, on off. Riaz blocks it back towards the bowler.
Tossed up, full and on off. Riaz digs it out towards extra cover.
The over ends with a single, three from it. This stand is trying to revive the innings.
This is sliding into middle and leg, Bismah Maroof flicks it through mid-wicket and rotates the strike.
A length ball, right around the top of middle. Maroof defends it out.
A touch wider and Riaz gets it through the point region for a single.
Fuller in length this time and around off. This is once again stroked towards the cover region.
A length ball, around the off stump. Riaz pushes it towards cover.
Fuller and around leg, Aliya Riaz gloves her attempted sweep shot down to fine leg for one.

Huge shout for lbw but nothing given. This is flatter and pushed through quicker around leg. Riaz looks to defend but the ball skids on and pings her on the pads. Alana King seems interested but they don't go for the review after the appeal is turned down. Probably missing the stumps and also pitching marginally outside the line of the leg stump.
A bit of excitement from the bowler but no pad involved. This is spilled down the leg side, very full and Aliya Riaz sweeps it towards deep backward square leg for a couple.
Full toss this time, Bismah Maroof steps out and drives it down to long off for a single.
This is angled across the left-hander, Maroof works it towards backward point.
Quicker and flatter, on off. Maroof hangs back and defends it out.
Fuller and on off, Aliya Riaz tries to defend off the front foot but does so off the inner half. It goes to mid-wicket.
Angling away from the batter, on a good length, Maroof taps it down to point and crosses for a brisk single.
A touch short and on off, angling in, Riaz gets back and tucks it in front of square leg for a run.
Width outside off, Aliya Riaz smacks it past the diving backward point fielder for a couple of runs.
On a length around middle, it's worked with the movement to mid-wicket.
Too full in length and outside off, Aliya Riaz digs it out to covers.
There is a slight drizzle out there at the moment. We hope it stays that way and doesn't get heavier. Also, Nicola Carey is now brought into the attack.
Loopy and full, around off, Bismah Maroof presses forward and defends it to the leg side.
Short and wide outside off, Aliya Riaz goes back and cuts it through point for a single.

EDGED BUT SAFE! FOUR! Tossed up, a bit short and around off, Riaz cuts hard and edges it behind. It flies past Meg Lanning at slip before she could even react. She tries to stick her hand out after taking evasive action but it scoots past her to find the fence at third man.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it to the off side.
Fuller and on off, swept behind square leg for a single.
Tossed up and outside off, Bismah Maroof goes back and plays it down to point.
Turning away from the batter, Riaz moves back and taps it down to covers.
Shortish and around off, defended to the off side.
Beautiful delivery and Aliya Riaz is beaten. Slower through the air, landing around off and spinning away, Aliya Riaz gets back to cut but misses.
A flipper, around off, Aliya Riaz goes deep inside the crease and punches it to covers.
Fuller and around leg, Aliya Riaz sweeps it down to fine leg for a brace.
Loopy and full on middle, it's pushed with the spin to covers.
Looped up again, full and on off, it's driven off the front foot but straight to covers.
Flighted delivery, full and outside off, Bismah Maroof drives but finds the point fielder.
Identical to the last delivery, this time, Aliya Riaz cuts it through point and rotates the strike.
Short in length and outside off, Aliya Riaz steps back and cuts but finds the backward point fielder.
Loopy one, full and down the leg side, Aliya Riaz sweeps it away fine down the leg side for a couple of runs.
Flighted and full around off, Riaz defends it off the front foot.

Drinks! One expected the spinners to have a field day on this pitch but the opening pair of Megan Schutt and Ellyse Perry did well to pick up wickets early on and Schutt was very miserly as well. With the dot balls rising up, the spinners have come in and King along with Amanda-Jade Wellington has piled on the misery. Bismah Maroof, the Pakistan skipper is playing a lone hand at the moment and she needs support in order to guide her team to a decent total.
Shout for an lbw, only from the bowler. Full and floated, around middle and leg, Aliya Riaz goes down and sweeps it to fine leg. They cross and it's given as a run. 50 up!
Tossed up, landing around off and turning away, Aliya Riaz steps back and cuts it to point.
Loopy and full on middle, Bismah Maroof kneels and sweeps it down to long leg for a single.
Flighted again, quite full and outside off, Maroof leans across and pushes it down to mid on.
Tossed up, landing around off and turning in, Bismah Maroof defends from the back foot.
Too full in length and around off, it's driven to covers.
A bit of flight again, wide of off stump. Riaz drives it towards the cover region.
Loopy delivery, around off. Riaz strokes it back to the bowler.
This is well dragged down, on middle. Bismah Maroof has time to get on the back foot and pull it down towards deep mid-wicket for another single.
Quicker and slanting across the left-hander. Maroof rocks back and cuts it straight towards point.
A bit flatter this time, outside off. Riaz opens the face of the bat and works it with the spin behind point for a run.
Loopy and full on off, defended off the front foot.
Floats it up, around off. Maroof pushes it back to the bowler.

Aerial but safe! Risky from Aliya Riaz but she gets away with it! This is drifting down the leg side. Riaz looks to sweep it behind square but gets a top edge on it. The fielder runs in from the deep backward square leg fence but can't quite get there in time. Single taken.
Around middle and leg, the sweep shot comes out now from Maroof. She doesn't quite get it off the middle of the bat but enough to pick up a single through mid-wicket.
Floated up, around the pads. Maroof flicks it on the leg side but can't find the gap.
This is tossed up again, a bit quicker and fuller, outside off. Bismah Maroof drives well but straight to the fielder at cover.
Loopy and full, around off, defended off the front foot.
Floated one, full and around fof, Aliya Riaz defends it with the spin to the off side. Amanda-Jade Wellington starts with a wicket maiden!
Aliya Riaz joins her skipper in the middle.

OUT! TAKEN! An excellent bowling change from Meg. Both leg spinners have got a wicket in their first over and Pakistan Women are in a spot of real bother here. This is nicely flighted again by Amanda-Jade Wellington, on off. Nida Dar is caught in two minds whether to come forward or rock back. Dar does come forward and pushes at it a bit early. The ball spins away slightly to take the outside edge and once again the Australian skipper Meg Lanning takes a comfortable catch at first slip. The spinners wreaking havoc at the moment.
Commentary.Howout: c Meg Lanning b Amanda-Jade Wellington

Commentary.Commentary: Almost bowled 'round the legs! This is looped up, down the leg side. Nida Dar gets low and looks to sweep but the ball comes off the gloves and hits the back pad.
Tossed up, outside off and turning away. Left alone by Dar.
Extra bounce now! This is bowled on a length, around off. The ball not only turns square but shoots up off the surface as well. Dar is left bamboozled.
Nicely flighted, on middle. Nida Dar watchfully blocks it out.
Bowling change. Meg Lanning makes another change. Amanda-Jade Wellington to have a go now. A slip in place.
Slower through the air and dragged down a bit. Maroof goes on the back foot and pushes it towards mid on.
This is angled into middle and leg, Maroof tucks it straight towards mid-wicket.
Around leg, tucked in the direction of fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Shot! Full and floated, landing around off, Nida Dar gets on the front foot and strokes it through the gap at extra cover for a boundary.
Around off, Dar strokes it towards cover.
Full, on middle. This is worked through square leg for a single.
Nida Dar walks in next to bat at number 5. Spin from both ends now, Jess Jonassen to bowl in tandem with King.

OUT! Cleaned up! Alana King with a wicket in her very first over! It looked like the wrong 'un but it was the normal leg spinner. On a length, drifted into middle and leg. The ball pitches and just skids through nicely. Omaima Sohail is late in her block and the ball goes through the gap between bat and pad and disturbs the stumps. The partnership that was brewing nicely for Pakistan Women is now broken. Shane Warne would have called it a natural variation of a spinner!
Beaten! On off, this is pushed through just a bit quicker and turns away ever so slightly. Omaima Sohail looks to cut but the ball beats the outside edge.
Drifted into middle and leg and turning away. Sohail defends it out of the front foot.
Full toss this time, on middle and this is dipping on the batter. Sohail pushes it back towards the bowler.
On off and this is swept away through square leg for a single.
King starts off with a fullish delivery, outside off. Maroof strokes it towards the cover region.
FOUR! Delightful shot to end Powerplay 1, Pakistan Women are 37/2! Ellyse Perry overpitches around off, Omaima Sohail leans into the drive and pierces the gap at cover-point for a boundary.

The umpire signals the start of Powerplay 2! The fielding side can now have up to 4 fielders outside the ring till the 40th over. Also, there is a bowling change, Alana King to bowl now. A slip, short cover and short mid-wicket in place.
Wide! Slightly short in length, around leg and angling further down, Sohail tries to flick but misses.
Around off, on a length, Maroof drops it with gentle hands to covers and pinches a single.
Short in length and on middle, Bismah Maroof turns inside the crease to pull but finds the fielder at backward square leg.
A low full toss around leg, Omaima Sohail tucks it behind square leg and collects a single.
On a length, around off, Maroof taps it down to point and takes a single.
A touch short and outside off, leaving the batter with the angle, Bismah Maroof pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Full again, this time on middle and leg, it's worked through square leg for a couple of runs. 6 from the over, much better for Pakistan Women.
Fuller and on off, driven to covers.
On a good length and outside off, defended to the off side.

FOUR! The gap is found finally and it's a boundary. Megan Schutt lands it a little too full, outside off and angling in, Omaima Sohail presses forward and drives it through the gap at cover-point for a boundary.
Back of a length, around off, Omaima Sohail stays on the back foot and steers it to backward point. Not finding the gap.
Fuller in length and wide outside off, Sohail drives firmly to the off side but fails to beat the diving cover fielder.
Full in length and outside off, left alone. Maiden from Ellyse Perry. Pakistan Women are going nowhere at the moment.

The plan seems to be to get the batter out driving. With a slip in place, Ellyse Perry drops it full and wide outside off, Bismah Maroof drives from the middle of the bat, but finds the cover fielder for the umpteenth time in this over.
Perry continues to pitch it up, it's around off again and Maroof does well to drive it through the line. Not in the gap though, again.
Lands it full, around off and angling away, Bismah Maroof leans forward and defends it solidly towards covers.
Pitches it up this time, around off, Maroof drives off the front foot to covers.
Digs it in short, around off, Bismah Maroof leans back and allows it through. It swings a bit on its way to the keeper.
Spears it in, full and on middle, Sohail leans across and forces it down to mid on. Just one wide from the over, it's been a quiet going from Pakistan Women.
Pitches it up and around off, it's pushed to covers.
Wide! Length delivery, quite wide outside off, Omaima offers no shot.
Fullish and on middle, slower in pace at 104 kph, Omaima Sohail offers a straight bat in defense.
Fuller and around off, Omaima Sohail drives it behind point but not in the gap. Yet another dot.
Beaten! A hint of away movement there. Megan Schutt lands it on a length and just outside off, Omaima Sohail feels for it and gets beaten.
A touch short and on off, Sohail goes on the back foot and punches it through the line. Finds the point fielder.
In the channel around off, angling away from a good length, Bismah Maroof covers her stumps and shoulders arms.
Wide! Sprays it short and way wide outside off, Bismah Maroof has nothing do with it.
Around middle, on a good length, Maroof defends it quietly to the leg side.
On a length and around off, Bismah Maroof covers the line and defends it towards covers.
Wide! Full and down the leg side, Maroof tries to flick but misses.

FOUR! Fine shot from the Pakistan skipper. Ellyse Perry pitches it further up and delivers it wide outside off, Bismah Maroof leans forward and crunches her drive through cover-point. Rachael Haynes gives the chase but the ball wins the race.
Too full in length and on middle, Bismah Maroof flicks again but finds the square leg fielder on this occasion.
Lands it on a fuller length around off, Bismah Maroof flicks but finds the fielder in front of square leg.
A huge in-dipper, starts from outside off and ends up on middle stump. Omaima Sohail defends it out. End of a maiden over from Schutt.
This is good bowling from Schutt, building up pressure with dot balls. This one nips back in from outside off and beats the outside edge of Sohail's blade yet again.
Length again but this is a bit wider. Sohail just dabs it down towards backward point.
Beaten! A length ball, shaping back in from outside off. Sohail tries to push it out but gets beaten past the outside edge.
This is pushed wide of off stump and Sohail lets it through to the keeper.
Nice shape from Megan Schutt! Fuller, on off and nipping back in sharply. Sohail keeps it out towards mid on.
On middle and leg, tucked away towards mid-wicket.
Length this time, on off and shaping back into the left-hander. Maroof stays solid in defense.
Full and wide, jammed out on the off side by Maroof.
FOUR! The Pakistan skipper is off the mark with a classy shot. Pitched up, on the pads and this is clipped in front of square on the leg side. The ball just races away to the mid-wicket fence.
Full, around middle and leg. This is flicked towards mid-wicket for a quick single.
Omaima Sohail is in next.

OUT! CAUGHT! Double breakthrough for Australia and it is a dream start for them! Almost the perfect delivery from Ellyse Perry as she bowls a length ball around off that angles in but just holds its line. Sidra Ameen is a bit caught on the crease as she doesn't quite know whether to come forward or go back. Ameen ends up pushing it out off the back foot but gets it off the outside edge. The skipper Meg Lanning takes an easy catch at first slip and it's a double whammy as both openers are now dismissed.
Commentary.Howout: c Meg Lanning b Ellyse Perry

Commentary.Commentary: Skipper Bismah Maroof walks in next. Meg Lanning has put two slips in place.

OUT! CAUGHT! Megan Schutt provides the early breakthrough for Australia! Schutt goes wider of the crease again and pushes it a bit fuller, well outside off. Nahida Khan is bound to come forward and drive at it but she does so a fair bit away from the body. Khan ends up pushing at it with hard hands and the ball goes straight into the clutches of Beth Mooney at gully. Some visible movement and extra bounce on that delivery brought an end to Nahida's stay.
Commentary.Howout: c Beth Mooney b Megan Schutt

Commentary.Commentary: Around off, driven to the left of mid off and the batters sneak in a quick single as the shy from the fielder missed the stumps at the bowler's end. Good running once again.
Schutt goes a bit wide of the crease and angles the ball in from outside off. Ameen taps it towards point.
Full and wide, this is kept out towards point.
Full again, on middle. Ameen pushes it towards mid on.
Full, around off and there's a hint of swing this time. Ameen jams it out on the off side.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries and this one's a bit lucky. Length ball, around off. Khan presses forward to drive but gets an outside edge which goes through the gap between first slip and gully for a boundary at third man.
MISFIELD AND FOUR! Lovely piece of timing from Nahida Khan. Overpitched, outside off and Khan just strokes it through the hands of the cover fielder and the ball races away to the fence.
A touch fuller and attacking the stumps this time. Khan punches it out towards mid off.
Perry pulls back the length this time and bowls it outside off. Khan just dabs it down towards the gully region more from the outer portion of her bat.
Pitched up, on off. Khan with a gentle push towards mid on.
Perry gets some swing right away. This is full and wide, curving away. Khan squeezes it out towards cover-point.
Ellyse Perry to run in from the opposite end.
This one slants into the pads and Nahida Khan is also off the mark with a tuck 'round the corner. Megan Schutt with a tidy first over, just 2 off it.
On off, this is pushed towards covers defensively.
Uppish but safe! Angled into middle and leg, Khan flicks it uppishly but just wide of the diving fielder at mid-wicket.

Good running! A touch fuller, around off. Ameen gets forward and drives it past the cover fielder. The mid off fielder cuts it off, to her left and they cross for a run. Sidra Ameen and Pakistan Women are off the mark now.
Length this time, angling in from around off. Ameen leans forward to defend it out.
Schutt starts off with a very full ball on middle. Sidra Ameen drives it nicely but straight towards mid on.

All in readiness here at the Bay Oval. The Aussie team is taking the field. Pakistan Women had a forgetful day with the bat and would be looking to turn things around. The conditions are looking ripe for batting and the pitch is going to be at its best in the first half. Sidra Ameen and Nahida Khan are the openers for Pakistan Women. Megan Schutt is getting ready to bowl. A gully is in place. Here we go...
Time for national anthems! Both teams have lined up in the middle. Pakistan's first and it's followed by the anthem of Australia. Nice to see the stadium bathed in the sunshine.

PITCH REPORT - Craig McMillan is pitchside and he is joined by Leslie Murdock. McMillan says that it is a bit warm and there is a nice little sea breeze blowing across the ground. Leslie Murdock adds that the surface won't be much different than the previous matches and it will be a run-fest and there's hardly any grass cover on it. Adds that spin will be key here.

Bismah Maroof, the Pakistan Women skipper, says that they are happy to bat first and will look to put on a good total on board. Adds that they have confidence in their spinners to defend the total and mentions that Javeria Khan misses out and Nahida Khan comes in place of her.

Australia Women captain, Meg Lanning says that they will have a bowl first and reckons that the pitch won't change much. She adds that they will look to build on the win and also informs that they have made a couple of changes with Darcie Brown and Tahlia McGrath missing out today.

Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Bismah Maroof (C), Sidra Ameen, Nahida Khan (In for Javeria Khan), Omaima Sohail, Nida Dar, Aliya Riaz, Fatima Sana, Sidra Nawaz (WK), Diana Baig, Nashra Sandhu and Anam Amin.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (WK), Rachael Haynes, Meg Lanning (C), Ellyse Perry, Beth Mooney, Annabel Sutherland, Nicola Carey (In for Tahlia McGrath), Jess Jonassen, Alana King, Amanda-Jade Wellington (In for Darcie Brown) and Megan Schutt.
TOSS - Up goes the flip of the coin and it lands in favour of Australia Women. They will have a BOWL first.

Pakistan were handed a thumping defeat in their opening fixture against neighbours and rivals India. After a decent bowling performance which could have been better as well given the fact they had India's middle order in a spot of bother, they certainly didn't step up with the bat. Despite being from the subcontinent, their batters really struggled against spin and Australia too have a couple of quality spinners. Pakistan are the underdogs in this match but anything can happen in a pressure situation in a World Cup match. Will the Aussies sweep aside Pakistan? Or is there an upset brewing on the cards? We'll find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

Australia are the favourites to win the trophy and a win in a pressure match against arch-rivals England in their first game of the tournament will only bolster their confidence further. The skipper Meg Lanning and Rachael Haynes were prolific with the bat and if Healy starts firing, the Aussies look unstoppable with the bat. Surprisingly though their bowling was not quite upto the mark in that win last time around and the experienced Jess Jonassen had to step up in the final over to see her side home. The likes of Perry need to find a bit of rhythm but young Tahlia McGrath and Alana King were really impressive.

The 2022 Women's World Cup is up and running and the games are coming thick and fast. After a rain-hit day in Dunedin on Monday, we now move to Bay Oval. In match number 6 of the tournament, Australia Women will take on Pakistan Women on International Women's Day. Both sides have had contrasting starts to their campaign and a win here will serve as a confidence booster for either side. On this note, welcome to the coverage.
